text:
hana: WFH confession 1: I mounted my router on the Peloton shelf because it has the best line-of-sight to the living room and my home office. yes, the bike is now my network appliance. photo: https://imgur.com/a/peloton-router (1 pic)
hana: neighbor stared at me through the window. i waved and said it's tech maintenance. :sweat_smile:
tom: iconic. does it survive sweaty cadence sessions? :bike:
ravi: how you power it? USB-C trunk from the power strip? risk level?
hana: short USB-C adapter, velcroed. wrapped in a small silicone mat so sweat doesn't drip on it. living on the edge.
becca: please tell me you have ventilation. routers + sweat = a sad combo.
hana: it's on a little makeshift bracket so airflow is fine. i've been running a 20-minute spin and monitoring temps.

ravi: ran an iperf after a ride, results below:
```
iperf3 -c 1.1.1.1 -t 10
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec  34.2 MBytes  28.7 Mbits/sec
```
ravi: solid for music + Zoom but video sometimes dips.

tom: poll: where would you hide a router temporarily? 1) Bike/sports gear 2) Closet 3) Bookshelf 4) Top of fridge
becca: 1 for novelty points.
hana: 1 until the bike becomes jealous.
ops-bot: Reminder: if device is moved to shared/common area, ensure SSID masking and guest network enabled for non-work devices. Use /net-config to update.
hana: enabled guest network and QoS for work devices. also labeled the cable so the housemate doesn't unplug mid-sprint.
tom: pls post a post-spin router pic. mandatory. :camera_with_flash:
ravi: also, name the guest SSID something scary so guests don't mess with it. "BACKUP_DNS_DO_NOT_TOUCH" works.
hana: will do. thanks for the sanity checks. if the router dies mid-class, i accept the consequences.
becca: if it becomes an official company product placement, we get a sticker pack.
ops-bot: Sticker eligibility: if router appearance generates >5 reactions, submit /swag-request for sticker sticker consideration.
